rewrites.title: Ex vivo stimulus washout and re-challenge in patient-derived primary cells
rewrites.description: Stimulate patient-derived monocytes, T cells, or fibroblasts with a defined AP-1-inducing signal, wash out for several days, then re-challenge and measure the speed and magnitude of AP-1 target gene induction (for example by RNA-seq time courses and nascent transcription). Memory is supported if re-challenged cells respond faster or more strongly than naive cells from the same donor, and the effect is abolished by a pharmacological AP-1 inhibitor or by a degron-based JUN knockdown.

rewrites.title: Mechanistic dissection of memory determinants with targeted perturbations
rewrites.description: Combine targeted epigenome editing (dCas9-based writers/erasers such as p300 or LSD1 fused to AP-1-bound loci) with mutations in the AP-1 binding motifs and in putative self-reinforcing partners (e.g., BAF complex, bromodomain proteins) to test which features are necessary and sufficient for persistence. If a chromatin mark at a single AP-1-bound enhancer can by itself reproduce or abolish the memory effect, this would establish a causal mechanism rather than correlation.

rewrites.title: Reanalysis of public datasets for AP-1 memory signatures
rewrites.description: Analyze existing ATAC, ChIP and RNA-seq data from trained immunity, wound-healing, neuronal activity, and epithelial inflammatory-memory studies. Test whether sites that stay open after stimulus withdrawal are enriched for AP-1 motifs and binding, and whether this predicts faster re-induction. Check for co-occurrence with pioneer factors (e.g., CEBP, ETS) and for histone mark persistence, providing low-cost (under $2k compute) evidence of generality across systems.

rewrites.title: Heritability of AP-1 state measured by clonal lineage tracing
rewrites.description: Use expressed DNA barcodes combined with single-cell RNA and ATAC profiling to ask whether cells sharing a recent ancestor also share high or low AP-1 target activity. Quantify how well barcode identity predicts AP-1 state as a function of generations elapsed, giving a direct estimate of the memory half-life in cell divisions rather than hours.

rewrites.title: Threshold comparison across graded stimulus doses or durations
rewrites.description: Expose cells to graded doses or durations of an AP-1-inducing stimulus (e.g., serum, TPA, injury, inflammatory cue) and use single-cell imaging or scRNA-seq to compare cells just above versus just below the activation threshold. Test whether a sharp jump in later enhancer accessibility and gene responsiveness appears at the threshold, which would indicate a switch-like memory rather than a smooth dose-response.

rewrites.title: Motif-specific enhancer editing and forced AP-1 recruitment
rewrites.description: CRISPR-mutate AP-1 motifs at persistently accessible enhancers to test necessity, and use dCas9-FOS/JUN to recruit AP-1 to naive loci to test sufficiency. Read out re-stimulation kinetics, accessibility, and H3K27ac, to separate AP-1 from other chromatin-based memory.

rewrites.title: Enhancer-level memory tested by re-induction kinetics
rewrites.description: Measure how quickly previously stimulated enhancers respond to a second stimulus, using CRISPRi or dCas9 blocking of AP-1 sites and CUT&RUN for H3K27ac and 3D contacts. The test is whether faster or stronger re-induction depends on enhancer marks that outlast AP-1 occupancy.

rewrites.title: Dimer-resolved binding and perturbation map
rewrites.description: Use CUT&RUN or ChIP-seq with antibodies or epitope tags for individual FOS, JUN, ATF and MAF members before, during and after stimulus. Combine this with paralog-specific degron depletion to determine which dimers mark and maintain remembered loci, so that results are not averaged across the whole family.

rewrites.title: History-dependence in pulse-train system identification
rewrites.description: Deliver randomized optogenetic AP-1 pulse trains with varying inter-pulse intervals and fit models of target output with and without a persistent state variable. If a memory term is needed, the response to later pulses should depend on earlier pulse timing with a decay constant that matches chromatin persistence rather than mRNA or protein half-life.

rewrites.title: Single-cell multiome and lineage tracing in vivo
rewrites.description: Use scATAC+RNA with lineage barcodes or AP-1 reporter/fate-mapping alleles in tissue such as skin wound repair, to follow descendants of previously AP-1-active cells. Compare their accessibility and function with those of AP-1-naive siblings, and test whether the memory is inherited through division and linked to AP-1 recruitment of BAF (SWI/SNF) and other chromatin remodelers.

rewrites.title: Pharmacological inhibition during establishment versus maintenance
rewrites.description: Use small-molecule AP-1 inhibitors (e.g. T-5224 or a JNK inhibitor) applied either only during the initial stimulus or only during the post-stimulus memory window, then assay the response to a later re-challenge. If blocking AP-1 during establishment abolishes memory but blocking it afterward does not, AP-1 establishes the memory; if blocking it during the window also erases memory, AP-1 is required continuously to maintain it, which distinguishes an establishing role from a self-sustaining state.

rewrites.title: Hysteresis and optogenetic dose-duration mapping
rewrites.description: Drive AP-1 with optogenetic or titratable inputs across ramp-up and ramp-down sweeps and varied pulse patterns, then measure output. Path-dependent output (hysteresis) or a persistent state would indicate feedback-based memory.

rewrites.title: Washout and re-challenge assay with AP-1 mutants
rewrites.description: Pulse cells with a stimulus, withdraw it, and track AP-1 target gene expression over time. Memory would appear as persistent expression after withdrawal and faster or stronger re-induction on re-challenge, which should be lost in AP-1 mutants lacking DNA binding or dimerization.

rewrites.title: Naive versus pre-exposed cell response comparison
rewrites.description: Prime cells with a transient stimulus, wash out, rest them, then challenge with the same or a different stimulus. Compare transcription kinetics (nascent RNA, PRO-seq) and amplitude against naive cells, and test whether the faster or stronger response at primed loci depends on prior AP-1 occupancy.

rewrites.title: Chromatin-versus-AP-1 uncoupling with epigenome editing
rewrites.description: Use dCas9-based tools to erase or install H3K27ac/accessibility at AP-1 motif enhancers, or mutate AP-1 motifs by base editing, and test whether memory follows the AP-1 site or the chromatin state. This separates AP-1 as the memory carrier from downstream chromatin marks that could be self-sustaining.

rewrites.title: Saturation mutagenesis of AP-1 sites in a barcoded synthetic reporter locus
rewrites.description: Integrate a library of barcoded reporter constructs carrying a minimal enhancer with variable AP-1 site number, spacing, and flanking sequence into a single landing-pad locus, then pulse, wash out, and measure barcode-resolved reactivation after days. This tests which sequence features are sufficient to encode persistent priming, separate from the native genomic context.

rewrites.title: FOS-driven tagging and reactivation of past-stimulated cells
rewrites.description: Place a FOS-promoter-driven, inducible Cre/tdTomato tag in cells during a first stimulus, then restimulate days later. Test whether tagged cells respond faster or stronger than untagged neighbors, using live imaging or scRNA-seq. Add AP-1 knockdown between the two stimuli to test necessity for maintaining the memory.

rewrites.title: AP-1 depletion after stimulus washout to separate AP-1 from its chromatin effects
rewrites.description: Stimulate cells, wash out the stimulus, then deplete AP-1 (dTAG or a dominant-negative such as A-Fos) after the transcriptional response has returned to baseline. Compare ATAC-seq, H3K27ac and re-stimulation responses with and without depletion, to test whether AP-1-opened chromatin keeps the memory after AP-1 has gone.

rewrites.title: Synthetic locus writing and release with dCas9-tethered JUN
rewrites.description: Tether a dox-inducible dCas9-JUN (and a DNA-binding-dead AP-1 control) to a naive reporter locus, withdraw dox, and assay independent dishes at a single fixed endpoint for reporter accessibility, expression, and inducibility. Persistence of an acquired permissive state after the tether is gone is a sufficiency test of whether AP-1 binding alone can install a self-maintaining memory at a defined site.

rewrites.title: Single-molecule residence-time tracking of JUN/FOS after pulsed versus sustained stimulation
rewrites.description: Use single-molecule tracking (HaloTag or SNAP-tagged JUN/FOS) to measure chromatin dwell times of AP-1 after a brief pulse versus continuous stimulation. If memory is encoded kinetically, cells with prolonged AP-1 dwell after a pulse should show persistent enhancer activity, and this dwell-time difference should predict the strength of later responses.
